Q: Splicing a template name into a variable declaration using CTAD A:

The C++26 draft explicitly supports class template argument deduction (CTAD) where the class or alias template is designated by a splice. See [dcl.type.simple]/3:

A placeholder-type-specifier is a placeholder for a type to be deduced ([dcl.spec.auto]). A type-specifier is a placeholder for a deduced class type ([dcl.type.class.deduct]) if either

  • it is of the form typenameopt nested-name-specifieropt template-name or
  • it is of the form typenameopt splice-specifier and the splice-specifier designates a class template or alias template.

The nested-name-specifier or splice-specifier, if any, shall be non-dependent and the template-name or splice-specifier shall designate a deducible template. A deducible template is either a class template or is an alias template whose defining-type-id is of the form

typenameopt nested-name-specifieropt templateopt simple-template-id

where the nested-name-specifier (if any) is non-dependent and the template-name of the simple-template-id names a deducible template. [...]

X is a class template, therefore it is a deducible template, and [:template_info:] is a splice-specifier that designates X, so it can be used as a placeholder for CTAD. Notice that this paragraph allows optional typename before the splice-specifier, but it doesn't allow template. The Clang implementation is correct.

Q: Convert a CodeIgniter query builer script into a raw MySQL query A:

Your model method uses CodeIgniter's query builder methods to render the following raw SQL assuming $id is the integer value 1.

SELECT *
FROM `t_trx_activity_detail`
WHERE `activity_detail_id` = 1

Your query builder script could have been reduced to:

return $this->db
    ->get_where('t_trx_activity_detail', ['activity_detail_id' => $id])
    ->result();

The query builder methods automatically escape and quote predictable entities. To identically replicate the same rendered query in CodeIgniter without query builder methods, a parameterized query is best practice.

public function per_id(int $id): array
{
    return $this->db
        ->query(
            vsprintf(
                'SELECT * FROM %s WHERE %s = ?',
                $this->db->escape_identifiers([
                    't_trx_activity_detail',
                    'activity_detail_id'
                ])
            ),
            [$id]
        )
        ->result();
}

If you don't need the table name and column name to be quoted, then it can simply be:

public function per_id(int $id): array
{
    return $this->db
        ->query('
            SELECT *
            FROM t_trx_activity_detail
            WHERE activity_detail_id = ?
            ',
            [$id]
        )
        ->result();
}

If you wanted to access the last executed query, you can call last_query().

$this->db->where('activity_detail_id', $id);
$resultObject = $this->db->get('t_trx_activity_detail');
echo $this->db->last_query();

If you want to see the current rendered state of a SELECT query in the query builder's cache, use get_compiled_select().

$this->db
    ->from('t_trx_activity_detail')
    ->where('activity_detail_id', $id);

echo $this->db->get_compiled_select();

If you want to dig deeper into the database driver cache from within your model scripting, there is a concise hack from PHP7 and higher.

Q: Python GTK+ 3 pull up just a file chooser dialog? A:

Here is a file picker that waits for a response and returns a filename or False (cancel) to a main class.
Change the print(fwin.fname()) line as needed to process the filename.

#!/usr/bin/python3
import gi,sys,os,time
gi.require_version("Gtk", "3.0")
from gi.repository import Gtk

class fnPick(Gtk.Window):    
  def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(title="FileChooser Example")
        self.dialog = Gtk.FileChooserDialog(
            title="Open...", parent=self, action=Gtk.FileChooserAction.OPEN
        )
        self.dialog.add_buttons(
            Gtk.STOCK_CANCEL,
            Gtk.ResponseType.CANCEL,
            Gtk.STOCK_OPEN,
            Gtk.ResponseType.OK,
        )
        self.dialog.connect("destroy", self.x_btn)

  def x_btn(self,widget):
        self.dialog.destroy()
        return False

  def fname(self):
        ans=False
        response = self.dialog.run()
        if response == Gtk.ResponseType.OK:
          ans=self.dialog.get_filename()
        elif response == Gtk.ResponseType.CANCEL:
          ans=False
        self.dialog.destroy()
        return ans

class MainClass(Gtk.Window):
    def __init__(self):
        Gtk.Window.__init__(self, title="qemu-mgr")

        #buttons
        btnbox=Gtk.Box(orientation=Gtk.Orientation.HORIZONTAL, spacing=50)    
        self.add(btnbox)
        clic=Gtk.Button(label='File')    
        clic.connect('clicked',self.f_click)
        exitbtn=Gtk.Button(label="Exit")
        exitbtn.connect("clicked",self.exit_clicked)
        btnbox.add(clic)
        btnbox.pack_end(exitbtn,False,True,0)

    def exit_clicked(self, widget):
      sys.exit()

    def f_click(self,widget):
      fwin=fnPick()
      print(fwin.fname())
      

win = MainClass()
win.connect("destroy", Gtk.main_quit)
win.show_all()
Gtk.main()

Q: Speeding up SPSC Queue on C++ A:

Related: What are the latency and throughput costs of producer-consumer sharing of a memory location between hyper-siblings versus non-hyper siblings? - with both threads sharing a physical core, in some cases you can get a lot more memory-order mis-speculation pipeline nukes. Check perf counters for machine_clears.memory_ordering (e.g. with perf stat under Linux). As reported on the linked Q&A, the OP there found a lot more machine-clears with HT siblings than across separate cores for that specific test.

I haven't looked at exactly what your benchmark does since there's no [mcve] of it in the question, only an off-site link. IDK how realistic it is, vs. a real use-case that does some real work between queue ops.

Over a millisecond as best-case latency sounds like something is very wrong.

Are you forcing both threads to run on the same logical core, so the OS has to context-switch between them? Rather than pinning them to separate logical cores of the same physical core which supports SMT (which Intel brands as Hyperthreading).

... Intel® Smart Cache refers to the architecture that allows all cores to dynamically share access to the last level cache."

That's just saying that Intel's L3 is a chip-wide shared cache. (Unlike AMD Zen where each cluster of 4 or 8 cores has its own L3, so data accessed by all cores has to be cached redundantly.)

So it seems that this is supported - or am I do not understand it?

If what is supported? Shared L3 cache? Yes, the CPU depends on that to work so there's no other mode of operation on a "client" chip (non-server, and not supporting multiple sockets.) The cores are connected via a fast ring bus.

(You say in the question your CPU supports 2 sockets, but no, https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/products/sku/199315/intel-core-i510600kf-processor-12m-cache-up-to-4-80-ghz/specifications.html confirms it only supports 1 socket. 2 sockets would also have meant you had 2 NUMA nodes. That page also confirms it supports Hyperthreading, 2 logical cores per physical core, making it a 6c12t CPU.)
